markers.label: WHO characterizes COVID-19 as a pandemic (11 March 2020)

sources.name: WHO Director-General's opening remarks at the media briefing on COVID-19, 11 March 2020

steps.title: March 2020: a pandemic
text: On 11 March 2020 the World Health Organization said COVID-19 could be characterized as a pandemic.
The map shows each economy's exports compared with the same month a year earlier. In March world exports were already **10.5%** lower.

steps.title: April–May: the plunge
text: World exports were **26% lower** in April 2020 than a year earlier, and **27% lower** in May. [India](IND)'s exports fell 61% in April, [Mexico](MEX)'s 57% in May, and [US](USA) exports 36% in May.
[China](CHN)'s exports, after falling early in the year, were 3% higher in April than a year before.

steps.title: A fast rebound
text: The recovery was much faster than after 2008. By December 2020 world exports were **8%** higher than a year earlier.
For 2020 as a whole they fell 7% to $17.6 trillion, then rose **27%** in 2021 to a record $22.3 trillion. The very large increases in spring 2021 partly reflect the low months of 2020.

steps.title: What grew
text: Some trade grew through the crisis. World exports of pharmaceuticals rose **9.2%** in 2020, to $682 billion, and of semiconductors 8.8%, to $867 billion.
The map shows the change in pharmaceutical exports from 2019 (CEPII BACI). Try Semiconductors & integrated circuits too.

steps.title: The cost in output
text: Real GDP fell **6.4%** in the [EU](EU) in 2020, 5.8% in [India](IND), 2.1% in the [US](USA) and 10.1% in the [UK](GBR). The [Chinese mainland](CHN) was among the few large economies to grow, by 2.3%.
The map is colored by real GDP growth in 2020.
